newsitem.title: UK: American Trust to become U.S. index tracker.
newsitem.headline: American Trust to become U.S. index tracker.

text.p: American Investment Trust said on Tuesday it planned to go ahead with changing to an indexation investment policy for its currently actively managed portfolio.
It said it would seek shareholder approval on June 5 for the change, which would see it tracking the S&P 500 Composite Stock Price Index.
If approved, it would be the only UK-listed indexed investment trust specialising in North America. At end January, the trust had a net asset value of 345 million sterling.

American said that it was concerned at the size of its discount to net asset value despite a narrowing over the last year, and believed a market opportunity existed for a trust tracking a mainstream U.S. index and that its shares should trade close to their underlying net asset value.

It said that based on the performance over the last 10 years of actively managed funds investing in U.S. equities, including American and UK pension funds focused on the U.S., it saw benefit in changing to tracking the S&P Composite.
"Furthermore the board believes that once the change to the company's investment policy has been implemented, there should be considerable demand for the company's shares," American said.

The need to change the portfolio would see the trust dispose of its investment in its fund manager, Edinburgh Fund Managers, and its Latin American holdings, which together represent about 5.7 percent of the company's portfolio.
The cost of the changed policy would be about 0.4 percent of net assets, while it would in future give shareholders an annual decision on whether the trust should continue.

Edinburgh has agreed to cut its annual management fee to 0.25 percent of net assets from the current 0.50 percent, and reduce the notice period on terminating its management contract to one year from three.
American would change its name to Edinburgh U.S. Tracker Trust Plc and could seek a global depositary receipt listing on SEAQ to broaden its shareholder base outside the UK.
If the changes are implemented, it said it would reduce the size of the board, with chairman Lord Macfarlane standing down at the end of September.
